title: 3 Steps to Build an EHR Governance Committee at a Rural Hospital
summary: A governance committee is an important part of rural EHR optimization after implementation. Learn the key steps toward building effective EHR governance.
body_markdown:
A strong governance process may identify more improvements than your team has the time and resources to implement. Limited IT capacity can make it difficult to keep your EHR current. The committee may also need guidance on EHR best practices or available capabilities.


[Cozad Community Health System](https://trubridge.com/resources/how-cozad-community-health-system-optimized-its-ehr-for-lasting-success/) (CCHS) in Nebraska experienced these challenges firsthand. It had a strategic governance committee but turned to


[TruBridge® Application Managed Services](https://trubridge.com/solutions/application-managed-services/) (AMS) for support.


“We really started seeing our governance grow with AMS as an extension of our team,” says


Erin Chytka, chief ancillary officer at CCHS


. “Our organization still owns the decision, but AMS brings the expertise and knowledge, helps us understand what’s possible, and executes the solution. The biggest benefit is that AMS allows us to redirect more of our internal time toward education and adoption than ever before.”


Outside expertise can extend your team’s capacity while your organization continues setting goals and priorities. It shouldn’t mean giving up local autonomy.
